name: Exact non-polynomial SAT demand/capacity separation schema

statement.latest: [\forall p\in\mathrm{poly},\;\forall N,\;\exists n\ge N:\;H_n(\mathrm{SAT}_n)>p(n)K_n]\;\land\;[\text{every correct size-}s\text{ SAT circuit has }H_n(\mathrm{SAT}_n)\le sK_n]\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathrm{SAT}\notin P/\mathrm{poly}\;\Longrightarrow\;P\ne NP
statement.note_ascii: if H_n(SAT_n)/K_n is not eventually bounded by any polynomial and universal circuit accounting holds, then SAT notin P/poly, hence P != NP

definitions.H_n: admissible non-circular semantic-demand quantity for the canonical length-n SAT function
definitions.N: arbitrary lower cutoff on input length

parents.evidence: The v0.1 route used the stronger eventually-dominates-every-polynomial condition. This refinement records the exact weaker condition needed to exclude a polynomial-size circuit family.

origin.source: Route-closure corrigendum to Semantic Closure Accounting for Boolean Circuits v0.1, 2026-09-11.

claim_boundary: Sufficient conditional schema only. No converse is claimed and the SAT-specific demand/capacity premise remains open.

name: Demand-Circuit Dominance route-closure theorem

statement.latest: [\forall C\text{ correct for }f_n:\;H_n(f_n)\le |C|K_n]\;\Longrightarrow\;H_n(f_n)\le CC(f_n)K_n;\qquad BK_n<H_n(f_n)\Longrightarrow B<CC(f_n)
statement.note_ascii: universal H <= circuit_size*K implies H <= minimum_circuit_size*K; any B*K < H is already a circuit lower-bound certificate B < CC(f_n)

definitions.CC(f_n): minimum correct circuit size for f_n in the declared finite circuit model

parents.evidence: The RRR demand/capacity inequality becomes a direct circuit lower-bound certificate once universal accounting is assumed for every correct circuit.
The theorem identifies that a super-budget semantic demand gap is already the transferred circuit lower bound, not an independent shortcut around it.

origin.source: Route-closure analysis, 2026-09-11; finite multiplication-only kernel formalized in the IDM P-vs-NP research branch.

claim_boundary: Finite meta-theorem only. It proves that the H/K route packages a circuit lower bound; it does not supply an admissible SAT-specific H_n or K_n and does not prove P != NP.

name: SAT Semantic Demand target — exact P/poly-strength refinement

statement.latest: \forall p\text{ polynomial},\;\forall N,\;\exists n\ge N:\quad H_n(\mathrm{SAT}_n)>p(n)K_n,\qquad\text{with universal sharing- and recomputation-aware capacity accounting for every bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit}
statement.note_ascii: for every polynomial p and cutoff N, some n>=N has H_n(SAT_n)>p(n)K_n, with universal sharing/recomputation-aware circuit accounting

definitions.K_n: to-be-proved universal semantic capacity scale per circuit gate

parents.evidence: The original target H/(K n^c)->infinity for every c is sufficient but stronger than necessary. This row records the exact non-polynomial-boundedness target needed for P/poly exclusion.
Demand-Circuit Dominance shows that proving this target together with universal accounting is itself an unrestricted circuit lower-bound breakthrough.

origin.source: Route-closure corrigendum to Semantic Closure Accounting for Boolean Circuits, 2026-09-11.

claim_boundary: OPEN. Registration records the exact target; it does not establish the target or change the public status of P versus NP.
